name: Wolfi
summary: Chainguard's container-first undistro: no kernel, glibc-based, packaged with apk, built from source, and released continuously.
patch_commands: apk update && apk upgrade   # in an image build, then rebuild and redeploy
patch_notes: Wolfi has no kernel of its own: a container uses its host's kernel, so `uname -r` reports the host. Fixes reach a workload when its image is rebuilt on updated packages.

identify.shows: Installed packages and versions in the image

eol.note: There are no numbered versions to reach end of life; rebuilding on current packages is the support model.

licence: Open source; the package definitions are on GitHub (wolfi-dev/os).

name: Flatcar Container Linux
summary: An immutable, container-optimized Linux that updates by writing a new image to a passive partition and swapping partitions on reboot.
patch_notes: New major releases start in the Alpha channel and are promoted to Beta and then Stable; the LTS channel gets bug-fix releases only. A reboot finishes each update, by default through `locksmithd` (Flatcar update and channel documentation).
advisory_notes: Each release's notes list its security fixes with CVE ids; the channel JSON carries the same notes per release.

identify.shows: Operating System, Kernel and Architecture lines (systemd hosts)

eol.note: Channel releases replace each other; there are no versions with published end-of-life dates.

licence: Community distribution; free to download. Each package keeps its own open-source licence.

name: Bottlerocket
summary: A Linux built to run containers, with no SSH server and no shell on the host: settings change through an API, and updates replace the whole filesystem image.
package_manager: None; whole-image updates through the Bottlerocket API
patch_notes: Run `apiclient` from the control or admin container. For EKS variants the project recommends the Bottlerocket update operator, and for ECS the ECS updater (Bottlerocket README).
advisory_notes: The oldest entries in the feed use GitHub advisory ids (`GHSA-...`) instead.

identify.shows: The host's settings through the API
From the admin container, a root shell on the host where `uname -r` and `/etc/os-release` can be read

eol.note: Releases replace each other; there are no versions with published end-of-life dates.

licence: Open source under the Apache-2.0 and MIT licences (Bottlerocket repository).

name: Kali Linux
summary: A penetration-testing distribution based on Debian Testing, published as dated snapshots of its kali-rolling branch.
patch_notes: kali-rolling is the default branch most users should run; it pulls from kali-dev once packages are judged stable (Kali Branches).
advisory_notes: Kali publishes no numbered security advisories. It imports most packages from Debian Testing as-is (Kali's relationship with Debian), so for the shared packages the [Debian Security Tracker](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/) shows each CVE's status in the testing suite. Fixes reach a Kali host through the kali-rolling branch.

eol.note: Snapshots are not supported separately; keeping kali-rolling current is the support model.
